title: Protocol 20 upgrade ledger: LedgerCloseMeta v0 with header 20 and 14 created Soroban config settings
why: The ledger that turns on Soroban is still a LedgerCloseMeta v0 (no generalized transaction set, no Soroban fields) although its header says Protocol 20, and its upgrade creates 14 CONFIG_SETTING ledger entries. Readers that pick the meta layout from the header version, or that ignore upgrade changes, misparse it or lose the network configuration.

variants.notes: Real pubnet ledger; header protocol 20, transactions applied under Protocol 19.

values.note: The LedgerCloseMeta arm is v0 (this pointer starts with /v0).

notes: 343 transactions (11 fee bumps) applied under Protocol 19. The 14 created settings, in order: eviction_iterator, state_archival, contract_cost_params_memory_bytes, contract_bandwidth_v0, contract_historical_data_v0, contract_events_v0, contract_max_size_bytes, contract_data_entry_size_bytes, contract_cost_params_cpu_instructions, contract_data_key_size_bytes, live_soroban_state_size_window, contract_ledger_cost_v0, contract_execution_lanes, contract_compute_v0; they are counted in expect.ledger.entry_changes. The next ledger, protocol-20/first-lcm-v1-generalized-tx-set, is the first LedgerCloseMeta v1. The lake object was written by stellar-core 23.0.1 long after the ledger closed (source.regenerated true), so its TransactionMeta is v4 with backfilled classic and fee events, not what a node emitted at the time.
